memory_candidates.content: Lean 4 pattern for generalising a concretely-instantiated proof over an inductive family to an arbitrary type-parameter: when the family has a typeclass-GATED constructor (e.g. SeqProof's `botL ... [IsIntuitionistic T]`), the only real obstacle to adding a `{T : Theory Atom}` binder is that gated arms must be RECONSTRUCTED, not merely matched. The idiom is `| _, @SeqProof.botL _ _ _ _ _ inst hbot, ... => letI := inst; botL ...` -- bind the stored instance via an `@`-pattern and rebind it with `letI` before reconstruction. Before assuming such a generalisation is a rewrite, look for an already-generic function over the SAME family in the same file (here `SeqProof.mono`): if one exists, it has already solved the gated-constructor problem and the port is mechanical rather than mathematical. The residual risk is not the binder but termination checking: a `decreasing_by` referencing an instance-specific re-export (`LJProof.height` for the generic `SeqProof.height`) is the most likely break point, so gate the generalisation with a scoped single-module build before touching anything downstream.
